scope: Confirmed CPU Stage materialization and source-loss scratch retirement

baseline.finding: Committed input targets survive Close, and successful StreamAgent materialization removes its journal without reclaiming the sealed local output. Neither path has a tested payload TTL or quota reclamation loop.

implementation.authority: Matching confirmed Artifact identity, version, digest, size and commit time for successful retirement; confirmed SOURCE_LOST disposition and persisted source-loss evidence for old output retirement. Production persists the accepted or replayed control response before either cleanup.
implementation.deletion_scope: The completed StageRun's input namespace and the exact manifest output under its own StageAttempt directory. Every directory component is opened and matched by inode; deletion stays relative to the exact bound StageRun and output-parent handles.
implementation.recovery: Materialization journal deletion follows successful scratch retirement. Lost control responses or failure to persist their confirmation preserve scratch and journal. A confirmed disposition is durable before deletion; partial cleanup or cleanup response loss retains it. After restart, confirmed records retry only local cleanup even after authority expiry. An unconfirmed SOURCE_LOST record repeats that report and never changes back to publication when the old output reappears.
implementation.command_identity: COMMIT and SOURCE_LOST persist a canonical command ID with the exact request evidence before sending. Retries retain the original ID and payload. An uncertain transport timeout retires the Connect stream; existing per-stream duplicate-ID rejection remains in force.
implementation.protection: Reject unconfirmed or mismatched Artifact evidence, another Attempt's locator, traversal, symlinks and changed output bytes. Preserve other StageRun/StageAttempt directories. Neither total-root replacement nor replacement of stage-runs, StageRun, StageAttempt or nested output-parent directories redirects payload deletion. Output leaves are opened with O_NOFOLLOW and checked by inode; directory pruning is nonrecursive.

compatibility.production_output_contract: Production explicitly selects attempt-owned-filesystem-scratch/v1 and validates the StageAttempt UUID locator namespace before requesting materialization authority. A nonconforming local sealed receipt and payload remain recoverable; no L2 publication or COMMIT occurs.
compatibility.generic_manifest: The generic LocalOutputManifestV1 parser and materialization authority issuer retain their safe relative locator semantics, including outputs/encoder.bin. Their existing fixtures are unchanged. Generic locators do not establish the unique ownership required by this filesystem retirement contract.
compatibility.journal: New workers write schema_version=2 and read schema 1 unconfirmed records or schema 2 records. A schema 1 record carrying confirmed_disposition is rejected. Old workers reject schema 2, so compatibility is forward recovery only.
compatibility.legacy_command_identity: Unconfirmed legacy records with committed_at or source-loss evidence but no original command ID are preserved with ErrLegacyMaterializationCommandIdentity. The worker does not guess a previous transport-generated UUID. Records whose terminal request was not prepared can acquire a new stable ID; already-confirmed records can finish local cleanup without a historical ID.
compatibility.rollback: Drain schema 2 recovery records with the new worker before reverting to an old binary. Drain legacy generic-locator records with their compatible worker before selecting the new production ownership contract. Do not erase fields, rewrite signed manifests or delete pending journals to force rollback.

non_success_lifecycle.committed_inputs: FilesystemInputTransferTarget.Close and Abort only remove pending transfer files. Completed input files from failed, canceled or expired StageRuns have no independent TTL or quota cleanup.
non_success_lifecycle.unsealed_output: H3 Stage mock cancellation and shutdown discard the current unsealed output. A ModelRuntime cancellation acknowledgment alone does not prove that compute has stopped.
non_success_lifecycle.sealed_source_lost: An accepted or replayed SOURCE_LOST report is persisted before retiring only the exact old StageAttempt output. The journal remains until cleanup succeeds, and confirmed recovery works after authority expiry. There is no independent local payload sweeper.
non_success_lifecycle.retry_boundary: SOURCE_LOST may move the same StageRun to RETRY_WAIT with a new fence. Its input namespace must remain available; the report does not authorize deleting that StageRun's inputs.
non_success_lifecycle.minimal_follow_up: Failed, canceled and expired StageRun inputs require a replayable terminal-state retirement authority plus proof that the runtime has stopped and no recoverable materialization remains. Do not derive deletion permission from mtime. Exact durable-result replay after unconfirmed control-response loss is supplied by migration 85 and stable journaled command IDs; unknown legacy random IDs require authoritative reconciliation.

The campaign exercises the same public retirement API after a real Materializer result; production StreamAgent integration has separate retry and restart regression coverage.

This change reclaims confirmed successful payloads and the old output of a confirmed source-lost StageAttempt. Inputs of retryable, failed, canceled or expired StageRuns remain until an explicit terminal retirement authority exists. It does not add general TTL or quota cleanup and does not establish that scratch is bounded for every failure campaign.
No retrospective scan deletes preexisting orphan files without completion evidence. Input transfer journals and other database or local evidence retain their existing lifecycle.
